what_worked: The build/buy/wait framework gives the deck a coherent strategic spine throughout.
fix_next: Replace garbled, illegible charts with accurate data visualizations anchored to verified dataset figures and proper category names.
verdict: Consulting-style framing over an empty analytical foundation with broken visuals.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: 'Total MRR $13.5M' — dataset shows $15.6M total 30-day revenue, not MRR; labeling as MRR is unsupported. Slide 2: 'Median MRR $282' — cannot be verified as MRR; dataset median is different from this figure. Slide 5: Categories 'Sales' and 'Security' are not in the dataset's category list; these appear fabricated. Slide 6: 'Entertainment' and 'Games' cited as high-growth markets — not present in dataset categories. Slide 7: Table is completely garbled/illegible with nonsensical numbers and text, making all data claims unverifiable and effectively fabricated.

evidence.insight: Recommendations are generic consulting advice (buy low-multiple companies, build in high-MRR markets, avoid saturated ones). No original analytical finding emerges from the data — no mention of revenue concentration quantified (49.6% top-10), provider landscape, anonymity premium, or B2B/B2C differences.
evidence.narrative: The build/buy/wait thesis is stated on slide 1 and returned to on slides 8-10, giving structural coherence. However, the middle slides (3-7) repeat the same point — acquire cheap startups — without building progressive evidence. Slides 6 and 9 largely restate earlier slides.
evidence.framing: Audience is named (founders, investors, corporate decision-makers) but scope, dataset provenance, limitations, and missingness (274 missing categories, 241 missing countries) are never mentioned. No definitions of 'MRR' vs. 30-day revenue. The 'revenue-verified' framing implies more rigor than shown.
evidence.accuracy: Total revenue mislabeled as MRR and wrong ($13.5M vs $15.6M). Categories 'Sales,' 'Security,' 'Entertainment,' 'Games' do not exist in the dataset. Slide 7 table is completely garbled with unreadable numbers. Slide 4 acquisition examples cannot be verified. No sample sizes, no missingness disclosure, no denominators given anywhere.
evidence.visual: Slide 5 chart has garbled axis labels ('MAZHUS,' 'MIRRKPLLACE') and unreadable values. Slide 7 table is entirely illegible gibberish. Slide 1 and 10 use decorative AI-generated illustrations that add no analytical value. Every slide follows identical Gamma template with 'Business insight' and 'Recommendation' blocks — highly repetitive. Slide 3 uses generic icon process diagram with no data.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive: every slide uses identical 'Business insight' / 'Recommendation' template structure. Decorative AI illustrations on slides 1, 7, 10. Garbled chart text on slides 5 and 7 is classic AI-generation artifact. Consulting buzzwords throughout ('bolt-on acquisitions,' 'GTM investment,' 'defensible differentiator'). Content is generic enough to fit any startup dataset.
